statement: For a Boolean event f on finitely many cell states, two product laws mu=product mu_i and nu=product nu_i satisfy |E_nu f-E_mu f|<=sum_i TV(mu_i,nu_i) P_Hi(S_i), where H_i has nu_j for j<i and mu_j for j>i, and S_i means the event is nonconstant in cell i for the fixed exterior.
assumptions: Finite state sets with the same cell skeleton in both laws
Independence of all cell variables within each endpoint law
proof_or_counterexample: Condition on the exterior of each telescoping replacement; constant sections contribute zero, and each other section differs by at most the one-cell total variation. Integrate and sum.
remaining_gap: G1: construct faithful model representations and prove their total weighted error vanishes. Parent C0017 is not proved.

statement: No finite undirected graph with three distinct terminal vertices and independent edges with probabilities strictly between zero and one induces a terminal partition law supported exactly on the all-separate and all-connected partitions with positive mass on both. For m fair edges in a graph connecting the three terminals, total variation from any such all-or-none law is at least 2^(-m).
assumptions: All-or-none target has all-connected mass p in (0,1)
proof_or_counterexample: If all terminals cannot connect, the all-connected mass fails. Otherwise a leaf terminal of a minimal spanning subtree is avoided by the path between the other two; opening exactly that path and closing every other edge has positive probability and produces a forbidden partial partition.
remaining_gap: This rules out exact finite independent-bond substitution only; it does not rule out approximate growing cells or prove G1.

statement: A three-edge independent star with edge probability 1/sqrt(2) matches all three pair-connection probabilities of a fair all-or-none site cell, yet the event that terminal a connects to b or c has probability 1-1/(2sqrt(2)), exceeding 1/2 by (1-1/sqrt(2))/2.
assumptions: Three mutually independent edges with common probability 1/sqrt(2)
Reference site cell joins all terminals with probability 1/2 and none otherwise
proof_or_counterexample: Pair probability is t^2. The one-versus-two probability is t[1-(1-t)^2]=2t^2-t^3. Substitute t=1/sqrt(2).
remaining_gap: Does not supply G1; shows that pair-matching alone cannot replace full connectivity comparison.

statement: Equal one-cell marginals do not control a joint crossing event if cell independence is removed: X=(Z,Z) and Y=(Z,1-Z), Z fair, have identical marginals but P(X_1=X_2=1)=1/2 and P(Y_1=Y_2=1)=0.
assumptions: The endpoint joint laws are the two stated dependent laws
proof_or_counterexample: Enumerate Z=0 and Z=1. Marginal distances are zero; the event-probability difference is 1/2.
remaining_gap: A dependent-block extension needs a justified conditional-kernel coupling or martingale argument.

statement: For the standard FK edge observable F(e)=E[exp(i sigma W_gamma(e,e_b)) 1_{e in gamma}], winding in radians, 0<sigma<1 and sin(pi sigma/2)=sqrt(q)/2, q=1 gives sigma=1/3, while sigma=2/3 gives q=3. The exact existing C0017 attempt card's standard-spin value 2/3 at q=1 is inconsistent with this convention.
assumptions: The explicitly stated standard FK observable and winding convention

source.existing_quote: for the q=1 FK model the parafermionic observable has spin sigma = 2/3

proof_or_counterexample: For q=1, sin(pi sigma/2)=1/2 and pi sigma/2 lies in (0,pi/2), hence sigma=1/3. Substituting sigma=2/3 instead gives q=4 sin(pi/3)^2=3. Local before/after residuals are in REPAIR_MEASUREMENT.json.
remaining_gap: Review the precise convention and apply the staged one-row correction; no scaling-limit theorem follows.

statement: If independent cell laws on a common skeleton represent the reference triangular-site and target square-bond crossing probabilities with errors r_mu(delta),r_nu(delta), and r_mu+r_nu+sum_i TV(mu_i,nu_i) P_Hi(S_i) tends to zero under the actual exterior hybrids, then the square-bond crossing probabilities have the same Cardy limit as the reference. This establishes neither the model-specific hypotheses nor interface convergence.
assumptions: All product-law and common-skeleton assumptions of w417-L1
Faithful marked-domain representations with the stated errors
The known reference triangular-site crossing theorem
proof_or_counterexample: Use the triangle inequality for the two representation errors and L1, then take the mesh limit of the reference crossing probability.
remaining_gap: G1 is exactly the unproved construction and vanishing-error estimate. No square-bond arm exponent or arbitrary-hybrid RSW bound has been assumed.
